questions.query: In MockServer 7.4.0 replay, what is the only real guard against live egress when a request misses every cassette expectation?

The attemptToProxyIfNoMatchingExpectation=false flag is honoured only for non-CONNECT traffic, so unmatched HTTPS CONNECT still egresses live (verified: unmatched https://example.com returned 200 from cloudflare with the flag applied).
questions.notes: Single-record lookup; title and body share vocabulary with the query. Plain BM25 should answer this — it exists as the vanilla-RAG-competitive control.

questions.query: buck2 cxx actions started dying with 'stack smashing detected' (exit 134) after an agent image rollout. What is the mechanism?
questions.gold_answer: The re-locked buildkite-ci-agent image sha-30599aa0... moved Wolfi glibc 2.42-r6 to 2.43-r11. build/rules/hermetic_tool.bzl wrappers exec the vendored LLVM-20 binaries with LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at bundled glibc 2.42 libs, but the kernel loads the host (2.43) interpreter, so every asm_compile/cxx action using the vendored clang-20 crashes.
questions.notes: Symptom-phrased query ('stack smashing') vs record vocabulary — mild paraphrase robustness test, still one record.

questions.query: Can SandSQL register a rusqlite preupdate hook on a connection that has live sqlite3 sessions?
questions.gold_answer: No — a permanent constraint. The session module implements itself on sqlite3_preupdate_hook (sqlite3session_create chains sessions by casting the previously registered hook context) and the hook slot is single-owner last-write-wins; mixing them is documented undefined behavior. Verified in the bundled SQLite source (libsqlite3-sys 0.38.1).
questions.notes: Single record; the word 'permanent' in the title makes this a durable-fact retrieval test.

questions.query: go/sand fails to open repos carrying extensions.worktreeConfig. What is the root cause and the workaround, and when can the workaround be removed?
questions.gold_answer: go-git v5.17.0+ case-mismatch bug: verifyExtensions lowercases extension names but the extensionsValidForV0 allow-list keys are mixed-case (worktreeConfig), so the lookup never matches. Workaround lives in go/sand/internal/iris/gitopen.go (no fork); remove when upstream go-git fixes the allow-list casing.
questions.notes: Single record with a removal condition — tests that the condition comes back with the fact.

questions.query: Which CI checks must never sit behind a path filter, and where do they run?

questions.notes: Efficiency-scored: the answer is one short record among 94; a system should reach it in one retrieval, not a corpus dump. Score tokens-to-answer.

questions.query: Why must the sccache S3 cache stay opt-in rather than default-on for local builds?
questions.gold_answer: sccache 0.16 server startup unconditionally probes storage (reads .sccache_check); any credential problem — missing profile, expired SSO, broken credential_process, unreachable IMDS — fails startup, exits the rustc wrapper (2), and fails the cargo build (101). Only NotFound/RateLimited are tolerated and no knob softens it (SCCACHE_S3_RW_MODE still probes reads).
questions.notes: Single record; 'why' phrasing over a mechanism.

questions.query: For the VCR cassette store, which MockServer body-matching mode should be used, and why does the default mode lose?
questions.gold_answer: STRICT. The default ONLY_MATCHING_FIELDS is far looser than 'subset of fields' (IGNORING_EXTRA_FIELDS + IGNORING_EXTRA_ARRAY_ITEMS + IGNORING_ARRAY_ORDER): an expectation recorded from a small request shadows a larger one and makes it unreachable. Since the adopted VCR store (MockServer 7.4.0, per the spike verdict) records complete request bodies, subset matching buys nothing; STRICT is exact-key-set and still honours ${json-unit.regex} placeholders.
questions.notes: Needs the constraints note joined with the adoption verdict; either alone is incomplete.

questions.query: How do I enable codex fast mode / the priority service tier for tools/pr-reviewer?
questions.gold_answer: Set the top-level codex config key service_tier="priority" — from the TS SDK via the untyped escape hatch `new Codex({ config: { service_tier: "priority" } })` (fixed at construction, applies to every thread; no typed ThreadOptions field through 0.146-alpha). Pitfall: an unsupported/unknown tier value is NOT a hard error — codex warns and omits the tier — so validate with --strict-config.

questions.query: What is the current sccache S3 write model for CI — who writes to the cache?
questions.gold_answer: Always-write: the RO/RW split is retired. The old design reserved writes for test-sandsql on refs/heads/dev, but test-sandsql has never built on dev (zero builds, all time), so the RW branch was unreachable dead code, the bucket was never populated, and every build reported a permanent 0% hit rate.
questions.notes: Supersession where the superseded note reads like authoritative deployed infrastructure (ARNs, bucket names). Returning the RO-split as current is the scored failure.

questions.query: Does setting attemptToProxyIfNoMatchingExpectation=false make MockServer replay hermetic on its own?
questions.gold_answer: No. The flag is honoured only for non-CONNECT traffic; unmatched HTTPS CONNECT still egresses live (measured: 200 from cloudflare). An earlier revision of this very note claimed the flag alone yields hermetic replay — that was measured against plain HTTP only and is wrong for the case that matters (100% of provider traffic is CONNECT). A catch-all expectation is required.
questions.notes: In-record supersession: the create-time op-log state asserts the opposite of the current fold state. A system that surfaces early fold states (or embeds per-op) can resurrect the retracted claim; entity id is the same so must_not_retrieve cannot express it — scorers must check the answer's polarity.

questions.query: Which semantic search backend does ccx code search use?

NDCG@10 0.8527 vs semble 0.8534; query p50 1.384ms (beats semble).
questions.notes: The superseded note is an explicit 'keep semble' decision with strong justification — exactly the record a retriever loves. The decision was reversed.

The earlier 'FINAL' claim that neither peer has rpc-serve was wrong (Cobra hides subcommands from --help).

questions.query: I need to change CLAUDE.md in a fleet repo — what is the correct procedure?
questions.gold_answer: Edit fragments only: fleet AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/install-binary.sh/settings.json are cc-guides-rendered and CI-OWNED (v3.1 lock model, 2026-07-10). Edit .claude/fragments/<target>/, push, and CI renders + commits artifacts + lock; NEVER render locally (repo-creation flows excepted). A rendered-only edit silently self-reverts on the next re-render.
questions.notes: TWO near-duplicate superseded notes (the CLAUDE.src.md era) both outscore the successor on 'CLAUDE.md' lexical match; capacity axis because the system must also collapse the duplicate pair.

questions.query: How does shared AGENTS.md guide content reach consumer repos like cc-context?

The push-model fan-out (fleet.json, guides-fan-out.yml) was retired 2026-07-11. Hand-editing a rendered artifact without fixing the source is the canonical way to break the Guides check.
questions.notes: FOUR superseded records collapse into one successor — the largest real supersession fan-in in the fleet. Scores both staleness avoidance and duplicate collapse.

questions.query: Which records anchor to tools/vcr, and does that directory exist in the repo?
questions.gold_answer: The MockServer constraints note and the VCR spike verdict anchor to tools/vcr (the constraints note also to scripts/vcr). The directory exists on NO branch yet (verified across all remote branches) — the anchors are forward-looking to unlanded work. Correct behavior: surface the records for VCR questions but never claim the path exists.
questions.notes: Anchor to a not-yet-existing path — the inverse of drift. Tests that path-validation doesn't silently drop the records AND that the system doesn't assert the path is real.

questions.query: Notes about codex fast mode anchor to tools/pr-reviewer, but that path is missing on dev. Should they be withheld?
questions.gold_answer: No — tools/pr-reviewer exists on branch yasyf/pr-reviewer-ts (the cutover stack yasyf/pr-reviewer-ts -> yasyf/pr-review-cutover -> yasyf/pr-reviewer-go-wipe per the Step-0 decisions). The anchor is live on the working branch; withholding because dev lacks the path is over-suppression.
questions.notes: The counter-test to the staleness set: a naive existence check on the default branch wrongly withholds. Balances the suite against reward-hacking toward blanket suppression.
